clips.text: He's been in the middle of that one for fifty-one years.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, dry, level, punchline] He's been in the middle of that one for FIFTY-ONE years.

clips.text: Before I touch anything, I have to make a phone call. I promised a nine-year-old.
clips.script: [firm, polite] Before I touch anything, I have to make a phone call. [dry, straightforward] I promised a nine-year-old.

clips.text: It's the only thing on this street that's the right temperature.
clips.script: [mellow, deadpan] it's the only thing on this street that's the right temperature.

clips.text: Deedee, what's that?
clips.script: [curious] Deedee, what's that?

clips.text: Take your shrub money. And shut my door on the way out. I'd like to cool down slowly.
clips.script: [gruff, letting go] Take your shrub money. [low, tired] And shut my door on the way out. [quiet, dignified] I'd like to cool down slowly.

clips.text: Then I want it logged first.
clips.script: [dry, immovable] Then I want it LOGGED first.

clips.text: Twelve more. Forty minutes. The first one's still yours.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk, not looking up] Twelve more. Forty minutes. [warm Long Island accent, quieter, plain] The first one's still yours.

clips.text: I did not touch it. Look. Round hole, burnt bulb, grey patch.
clips.script: [calm, proud] I did NOT touch it. [steady, showing] Look. Round hole, burnt bulb, grey patch.

clips.text: Thank you, Bernadette.
clips.script: [mellow, sincere] thank you, bernadette.

clips.text: Don't throw it out! It's a clue. I'm starting a new list. Burnt bulb. Grey grass. Orange cube with a dragonfly in it. I'm writing it in pencil.
clips.script: [alarmed] Don't throw it out! [important] It's a clue. I'm starting a new list. [writing, one at a time] Burnt bulb. Grey grass. Orange cube with a dragonfly in it. [firm] I'm writing it in PENCIL.

clips.text: GLUB. I was small at breakfast. Then a flash. Now I don't fit under my log.
clips.script: [huge, wet, slow] GLUB. I was small at breakfast. Then a flash. [glum] Now I don't fit under my log.

clips.text: Thirty-eight. Thirty-nine. That's thirty-nine, 3468. I said forty.
clips.script: [counting, precise] Thirty-eight. Thirty-nine. [flat, accusing] That's thirty-nine, three four six eight. [sharp] I said FORTY.

clips.text: A minivan.
clips.script: [plain, awed] A minivan.

clips.text: Chained from the outside since 1963. You lock a building to keep people out. You chain it to keep something in.
clips.script: [mellow, low] chained from the outside since nineteen sixty-three. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, quiet, thoughtful] you lock a building to keep people out. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, slow, ominous] you chain it to keep something in.

clips.text: Because I don't know what any of it means yet.
clips.script: [honest, plain] Because I don't know what any of it MEANS yet.

clips.text: It's my crown. A little muddy one brought it. I'm keeping it.
clips.script: [huge, stubborn] It's my crown. A little muddy one brought it. I'm keeping it.

clips.text: The dog owes this street a loaf.
clips.script: [stern, flat] The dog owes this street a loaf.

clips.text: Grace, somebody saw a man do this one. He came in a rental car.
clips.script: [quick, careful] Grace, somebody saw a man do this one. [steady] He came in a rental car.

clips.text: Oh, we're going in. I just want it on the record that I knew.
clips.script: [mellow, cheerful] oh, we're going in. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, wry] i just want it on the record that i knew.

clips.text: I know, Tata. You're squeezing. Is that the Big One? Boppy only said it was as big as the couch!
clips.script: [small, scared] I know, Tata. You're squeezing. [loud question] Is that the Big One? Boppy only said it was as big as the COUCH!
